Context note: we run 24 regional pods handling 18,000 req/s during peak UTC afternoon windows. When a new hostname is queried before its DNS record propagates, recursive resolvers cache the NXDOMAIN response for the SOA minimum TTL (often 5–60 minutes). Even after the A/CNAME record is published seconds later, clients behind those resolvers continue failing until the negative TTL expires. Pre-provisioning DNS records before traffic shifts and keeping SOA negative TTLs short (30–60 seconds) avoids prolonged lockouts.
